svg.aria-label: The DNSSEC chain of trust from the root key to net's key to ripe.net's key to a signed A record

g.text: 🔑 the root’s key (built into every validating resolver)
DS for net.: “net’s key has this fingerprint”
Every link checks, so the resolver sets the “ad” flag: authenticated data.

ol.li: Every validating resolver has the root zone’s public key built in: the one thing it must trust. The root signs a record for each top-level domain that uses DNSSEC: a DS record, the fingerprint of that domain’s own key.
The net servers publish their key, which matches the fingerprint the root signed. They sign a DS record for each signed domain under them, like ripe.net. (The real one, from dig DS ripe.net.)
RIPE’s servers publish their key, which matches that fingerprint, and sign every record in their zone. With the answer comes an RRSIG: the signature.

A forged answer would need a signature made with RIPE’s private key, which only RIPE has. And nobody can swap RIPE’s key for their own, because net vouched for the real one, and the root vouched for net’s.

figure.figcaption: DNSSEC: a chain of signatures from the root to the answer.
